title: Ports, environment and flags
summary: Publish ports with -p, configure with -e, and use -d, --rm and --name well.

steps.title: Publishing ports
body: Each container has its **own network stack**. A web server listening on port 80 inside the container is listening on the *container's* port 80, not your laptop's. To reach it from the host you **publish** a port:
```text
docker run -d -p 8080:80 nginx:1.27
│    └── container port (where the app listens)
└─────── host port (what you type in the browser)
browser ──▶ localhost:8080 ──▶ [ Docker ] ──▶ container:80 ──▶ nginx
- `-p 127.0.0.1:8080:80` publishes on the loopback address only, so other machines cannot reach it.
- `-P` publishes every `EXPOSE`d port on a random high host port.
- `EXPOSE 80` in a Dockerfile is **documentation**. It publishes nothing on its own.
- Only one thing can own a host port: a second `-p 8080:...` fails with *port is already allocated*.

steps.prompt: You ran `docker run -d -p 5050:80 nginx:1.27`. Which URL shows the nginx welcome page in your browser?
steps.explain: Host port first, container port second. The browser talks to the host port.

steps.prompt: With the given command or Dockerfile, can a browser on the **host** reach the app inside (listening on 0.0.0.0:80)?
items: `docker run img` with `EXPOSE 80` in the Dockerfile
steps.explain: Only publishing (`-p` or `-P`) opens a path from the host. The last one publishes container port 8080, but the app listens on 80.

steps.title: Environment and the other everyday flags
body: Images should be **configured at run time**, not rebuilt per environment. The usual way is environment variables:
```text
docker run -e ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Staging -e Db__Host=db acme/api:1.4
docker run --env-file ./staging.env acme/api:1.4
Other flags you will type every day:
| flag | meaning |
| `-d` | detached: run in the background and print the container ID |
| `--name api` | a fixed name instead of a random one like `quirky_turing` |
| `--rm` | delete the container automatically when it exits |
| `-it` | interactive with a terminal, for shells and REPLs |
Anything **after the image name** is the command to run instead of the image's default, and its arguments: `docker run --rm alpine ls /etc` runs `ls /etc`.

steps.code: docker run --rm -e GREETING=hello alpine sh -c 'echo $GREETING world'
steps.explain: The single quotes stop *your* shell from expanding `$GREETING`; `sh` inside the container expands it from the environment Docker set.

steps.prompt: Match each flag to what it does.
pairs: returns immediately; the container runs in the background
removes the container when its main process exits
sets an environment variable inside the container
forwards host port 8080 to container port 80
gives the container a predictable name

steps.prompt: Run PostgreSQL in the background as `db`, with a password, reachable on host port **5433** (Postgres listens on 5432).
steps.explain: Host side first: `5433:5432`. Using a different host port is a common trick when a local Postgres already owns 5432.

steps.prompt: `docker run -d -p 8080:80 nginx` fails with `Bind for 0.0.0.0:8080 failed: port is already allocated`. What is the most likely cause?
options: Another container (or program) on the host already uses host port 8080
nginx cannot listen on port 80 inside a container
Port 8080 must be declared with EXPOSE first
The image name needs a tag
steps.explain: Find it with `docker ps` (look at PORTS), then stop it or publish on another host port such as `-p 8081:80`.

steps.title: Explain a docker run command
prompt: Write `List<string> ParseRun(string command)` that explains a `docker run` command line. Tokens are separated by spaces (no quoting). Read the tokens after `docker run`:
- `--name X`, `-p SPEC`, `-e KEY=VALUE` take the next token (`-p` and `-e` may repeat)
- the first other token is the **image**; everything after it is the **command**
command: (image default)          (or the remaining tokens joined by spaces)
A port spec `A:B` prints `A -> B`; `IP:A:B` prints `IP:A -> B`.
template: Dojo.Eq("a detached web server", new List<string> { "image: nginx:1.27", "name: web", "detached: yes", "remove on exit: no", "ports: 8080 -> 80, 127.0.0.1:9000 -> 9000", "env: MODE=prod", "command: (image default)" }, ParseRun("docker run -d --name web -p 8080:80 -p 127.0.0.1:9000:9000 -e MODE=prod nginx:1.27"));

Dojo.Eq("a one-off command", new List<string> { "image: alpine", "name: (random)", "detached: no", "remove on exit: yes", "ports: none", "env: A=1, B=2", "command: ls -la /etc" }, ParseRun("docker run --rm -it -e A=1 -e B=2 alpine ls -la /etc"));

Dojo.Eq("flags after the image belong to the command", new List<string> { "image: acme/tool", "name: (random)", "detached: no", "remove on exit: no", "ports: none", "env: none", "command: -d --verbose" }, ParseRun("docker run acme/tool -d --verbose"));
hints: Walk the tokens with an index starting at 2, so you can consume the next token with `t[++i]`.
Stop the flag loop as soon as you have found the image; everything after is the command (`t.Skip(i)`).
A `-p` spec split on `:` has 2 parts, or 3 when it starts with an IP.
